hypotheses.construction_plan: Instantiate the two-slot kernel T(u,v) at the ordered pair (u,v)=(i,j). Apply identity to obtain T(i,j); apply the S2 permutation operator to swap arguments and obtain T(j,i). The full expression is the S2-orbit sum (identity + permute)[T(u,v)] evaluated at (i,j).
required_assumptions: T is a binary function with two ordered argument slots
The permutation operator exists and acts by swapping the two arguments
hypotheses.rationale: The non-trivial structural variation among the subterms is reversal of the argument list of the same binary function T. This is exactly the action of the two-element permutation group on the ordered index pair, and group averaging under that action reproduces the raw sum as a symmetric combination without assuming T itself is symmetric.
